endorsements.quote: First, AI tools should demonstrate their efficacy and safety, similar to Chambless and Hollon’s standard of efficacy [ 18 ].
Third, Chambless and Hollon [ 18 ] emphasized the importance of identifying in which populations and settings the treatment was tested.
Finally, we add that any use of AI should provide proof of its adherence to laws, such as Public Act 104‐0054 and the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).

Equally important, the system must include a clear and understandable consent process for patients, detailing what data will be processed, how it will be used, and under what circumstances it might be shared.

unlisted_practices: Require AI tools for mental health to demonstrate fidelity to their intended function, with expert clinicians screening sample conversations against an 80%-100% fidelity benchmark.
Require two or more RCTs or strong single-case designs showing AI mental health tools are superior or equivalent to an established treatment, with an empirical demonstration of no harm.
Pay special attention to language, cultural factors, and digital literacy when evaluating AI mental health tools.
Establish standards for when updates to underlying AI systems require retesting of fidelity and efficacy.
Develop standards of evidence for mental health AI tools that could be adopted by states pairing statutory boundaries with operational criteria.
Clarify statutory boundaries for gray-area AI functions, such as psychoeducation, session summaries, and risk-flagging, and provide an explicit research exemption.
Include mechanisms for auditing and updating AI systems as laws evolve, treating legal compliance as an ongoing requirement.
Require AI tools that process session transcripts to show that data are stored securely, accessible only to authorized clinicians, and deleted per retention policies.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/framework paper analyzing a state statute (Illinois PA 104-0054) and proposing a framework for evidence, safety, and legal compliance for AI tools in mental health.
